  "endpoint_class": "not-stated",
  "concordance_definition": "The study defines concordance implicitly by examining the overlap between diseases investigated by GWAS and diseases investigated in drug development, and by comparing drug targets with genetic support to successful drug development programs.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "The number of terms in the DO may be incomplete and not capture all medical conditions.",
    "The analysis focused on common polygenic human diseases, excluding rare loss-of-function variants causing monogenic disorders.",
    "Trait and indication mappings from GWAS Catalog and ChEMBL may lack granularity (e.g., general indications like 'digestive system diseases').",
    "Further efforts are needed to harmonize disease ontologies used in GWAS and drug development.",
    "GWAS performed but not publicly disseminated would underestimate the number of existing diseases studied in GWAS.",
    "Assigning genetic associations from GWAS data to a causal gene remains a challenge due to linkage disequilibrium.",
    "The concept of the 'druggable genome' is evolving.",
    "Information on drugs in development may be incomplete or inaccessible for commercial reasons, potentially underestimating diseases studied in drug development, especially for preclinical candidates.",
    "Some diseases could have been studied through a validated clinical biomarker not captured by the approach.",
    "Disease prevalence was not considered.",
    "Mortality or morbidity were not considered.",
    "Many diseases are not tractable by therapeutic agents (e.g., congenital malformations) and require surgical or device-based treatments.",
    "Key targetable mechanisms may no longer be usefully targeted by the time the disease is manifest.",
    "Not all human diseases may need to be treated with a therapeutic intervention."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": null,
  "key_numbers": [
    "5% of the diseases have an approved drug treatment in at least one region of the world.",
    "Less than half of the diseases that pharmaceutical companies are currently attempting to develop drugs for have been investigated by GWAS.",
    "Approximately two-thirds of the diseases investigated using genetic studies have yet to be investigated in drug development.",
    "As of 29 September 2022, the Human Disease Ontology (DO) had 11,158 disease terms.",
    "The total number of protein-coding genes in the human genome is estimated at 19,813.",
    "4729 encode proteins estimated to be amenable to targeting by small molecule drugs or bio-therapeutics.",
    "755 (16%) of all human genes encoding druggable targets are already the targets of approved drugs.",
    "1218 (26%) are the targets of drugs in clinical development.",
    "418 (9%) are targets of drugs in preclinical development.",
    "3495 (73.9%) are currently ‘undrugged’.",
    "1549 unique diseases (estimated as 13.9% of the total number of human diseases in DO) have an approved drug and/or a drug under clinical or preclinical development.",
    "612 diseases are the indication of approved drugs.",
    "1401 diseases are or have been the indication of drugs in clinical development.",
    "210 diseases are or have been indications for drugs in preclinical development.",
    "1914 diseases covered by GWAS (17.2% of the total number of common human diseases).",
    "Of the 1549 diseases with an approved treatment and/or a treatment that is or has been investigated in clinical or preclinical development, 703 had also been investigated by GWAS.",
    "1211 diseases have been the subject of investigation in GWAS, but have yet to be investigated in drug development.",
    "19,813 protein-coding genes and 11,158 diseases produce ~221 million protein-disease indication pairings.",
    "4729 genes encoding druggable targets and 11,158 human diseases produce ~52.8 million drug target-disease indication pairings.",
    "1218 genes encoding the targets of drugs and 1401 diseases for which these targets are being or have been investigated in clinical phase drug development, giving around 1.7 million target-indication pairings.",
    "Within this bounded space of ~1.7 million target indication pairings, only 42,199 unique target-indication pairings (2.5%) have been explored in drug development.",
    "755 targets of approved drugs for 612 disease indications, giving a sample space of 462,060 target indication pairs.",
    "Of these, 5221 drug target-disease indication hypotheses have been explored and led to approval (1% of the maximum space).",
    "37 genes encoding approved drug targets for the treatment of hypertension.",
    "The median number of drug targets per approved indication is two.",
    "The glucocorticoid receptor is employed as a drug target for the treatment of around 111 diseases.",
    "755 targets of currently approved drugs (16% of all druggable targets) employed in the treatment of 612 diseases (5.5% of all 11,158 diseases).",
    "Of these diseases, 336 have also been studied in GWAS.",
    "The 1234 targets of drugs that are or have been the subject of clinical investigation have been or are being evaluated for the treatment of 1549 diseases.",
    "Of the 1401 disease indications being evaluated in clinical development, only 661 have previously been the subject of a GWAS.",
    "Of these 1401 disease indications, 476 have already approved treatment, and of the remaining 925 diseases, 363 have been studied by a GWAS.",
    "Only a small fraction of the 11,158 diseases curated in the human DO have been investigated in drug development (14%; 1549 out of 11,158 diseases) or GWAS (17%; 1914 out of 11,158 diseases).",
    "Of diseases being pursued in clinical phase drug development, only 47% have been the subject of a GWAS (661 out of 1401).",
    "11,158 diseases in the DO were used as the denominator.",
    "ICD-10 includes 12,318 diseases.",
    "Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) includes 16,601 diseases.",
    "Only 17% of human diseases have been investigated in a GWAS.",
    "Over 8000 diseases exist without an approved treatment or under clinical investigation."
  ]
}
